title: Precision-agnostic execution proxy and kernel handoff to minimize dequant/requant overhead
creator: Maya Chen
description: We observe significant tail latency and token-cost regressions caused by repeated dequant/requant transitions during mixed-precision prefill and decode. This ticket implements a precision-agnostic execution proxy (PAEP) that mediates between the scheduler and kernel implementations. PAEP tracks tensor precision metadata, negotiates zero-copy kernel handoffs, and applies ephemeral view semantics to avoid materializing full dequantized tensors when kernels can accept quantized views or perform fused on-the-fly ops. Goals: 1) reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead from dequant/requant, 2) enable a graceful handoff path when mixed-precision kernels are available for a subgraph, and 3) provide observability hooks to measure handoff frequency and avoided copies.
acceptance_criteria: PAEP design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra (arch review)
Prototype integrated into prefill pipeline for decoder+KV path with feature flag
End-to-end latency for 2048-token streaming scenario reduced by >=6% median and >=10% p95 compared to baseline with eager dequant
End-to-end per-token GPU memory copies reduced by >=30% in workloads with <10% cross-layer precision mismatches
Fallback correctness tests cover all model shapes used in our catalog and pass CI
Telemetry emitted: handoff_count, avoided_copy_bytes, fallback_reasons (string tag)
No customer-facing behavior changes when feature flag is off
notes: Initial spike analysis: conv/dequant ops account for ~12-18% of decode latency on Llama-variant models at batch=1, seq=1024.
Trade-off: aggressive zero-copy may complicate kernel memory lifetime and GC; choose ephemeral views with explicit ownership transfer semantics.
Policy: per-layer manifest will contain preferred execution precision and a compatibility score to assist scheduler decisions.
We prefer a lightweight proxy that performs metadata-only negotiation; heavy rewrite of kernel APIs avoided in v1.
Security: the proxy will not change tensor contents; KMS/HSM concerns not applicable for this layer but audit hooks should exist for private deployments.

implementation_plan: 1) Finalize handshake API between scheduler and PAEP (metadata only).
2) Implement ephemeral tensor view type and ownership transfer semantics in runtime/core/tensor_views.
3) Add kernel adapter stubs for INT8 and FP8 paths that accept views and expose 'capabilities' flags.
4) Wire feature flag into prefill and decode path; run microbench suite across representative models.
5) Emit telemetry and lightweight tracing spans for each handoff decision.
6) Rollout: start with internal canary on staging DED clusters, then gated rollout to production with monitoring thresholds.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect lifetime handling could corrupt KV cache. Mitigation: strict unit tests and a debug mode that enforces copy semantics.
Risk: little benefit for models with pervasive precision mismatches. Mitigation: metric-driven rollout and per-model opt-out.
Risk: increased scheduler complexity. Mitigation: keep PAEP as metadata-only negotiator; do not embed heavy heuristics in v1.
